title: Grateful Dead Live at The Crystal Ballroom on 1968-02-03
lineage: SBD > MR > DAT > Sonic Solutions > CD > SHN > shntool > mkwACT > SHN (seekable)

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture of early ’68 delivers crystal‑clear guitars and drums while showcasing a fiery set highlighted by China Cat Sunflower→The Eleven, a tight Cryptical > The Other One suite and the rare Born‑Crossed‑Eyed.
ai_review.review: This tape is a classic snapshot of the Dead’s transition to acid‑driven improvisation.  The soundboard source provides surprisingly clear guitar and drum definition for a 1968 recording, though the mix can feel a little thin in places.  Musically the show is high‑energy – standout moments include the blazing China Cat Sunflower into The Eleven, a tight Cryptical > The Other One run, and an electrifying New Potato Caboose with Pigpen’s organ soaring.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly positive reviews praise the performance and highlight many classic jams; recording quality is noted as good for its era with minor mix issues, yielding a strong combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Guitars and drums are clear for an old tape; some listeners note a C/C+ sound quality and a slight speed/tempo perception, but overall the board mix is listenable with occasional vintage tape hiss.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Typical early‑68 set with strong transitions, especially the fiery China Cat Sunflower → The Eleven and a tight Cryptical > Other One suite that keeps the momentum high.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar tone is praised (even likened to Duane Allman) and described as clear, powerful, and central to the jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir’s vocals receive compliments, noted as especially strong on tracks like Clementine.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ shines in The Other One suite and New Potato Caboose, often louder than later mixes and adding vivid color.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drummers create swirling grooves; Mickey Hart’s influence is highlighted in the complex, energetic feel of The Eleven.
